question: On 5 August 2024 phone apps showed the week on Wall Street like this, and headlines spoke of a crash. Where's the trick?
answer: In the axis, drawn from 5,150 to 5,550, so a 6% dip fills the screen as an 80% one would. Most finance apps zoom to fit the wiggle. Within weeks the index had recovered, and 2024 closed up 23%. Anyone who sold at the bottom of that screen sold at the week's low.
move: Before reacting to a fall, ask what share of the whole it is.
ask: When my savings app shows a drop, do I check its size against the whole?

scene.headline: Global stocks crash
scene.label: S&P 500 at the close
scene.found: Yes: the axis covers only 400 points of a 5,500 index.
scene.miss: That part is fair. Look at the range the axis covers.

misses.headline: The papers did say so. Does the drawing show the size?
misses.marks: The closes are right. It's the ruler they hang on.

scene.name: The zoomed axis
scene.lesson: Apps zoom the axis to fit the wiggle. Compare a fall with the whole before you panic.

source: S&P Dow Jones Indices, S&P 500 closes
reference: S&P Dow Jones Indices, S&P 500 daily closing levels, 31 July to 9 August 2024, and 2024 year-end close (5,881.63, against 4,769.83 at the end of 2023)
